Let \(f(x,y)=\sqrt7 x-y\). On the circle \(x^2+y^2=\frac94\), the maximum and minimum of \(f\) are
\[
\pm \sqrt{7+1}\cdot \frac32=\pm 3\sqrt2.
\]
Thus \(\sqrt7 x-y\) ranges over \([-3\sqrt2,3\sqrt2]\). Maximize
\[
|\sqrt7 x-y-\sqrt2|
\]
over this interval. The farthest from \(\sqrt2\) occurs at \(-3\sqrt2\):
\[
|-3\sqrt2-\sqrt2|=4\sqrt2.
\]
So
\[
d_{\max}=\frac{4\sqrt2}{\sqrt{7+1}}=\frac{4\sqrt2}{2\sqrt2}=2.
\]

\[
\boxed{2}
\]
